mainEntity.name: Do you provide assisted living & senior living cleaning in Littleton, MA?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Littleton (Middlesex County) is one of the 109 Massachusetts cities and towns we serve. It is about 14 miles north of our Marlborough base in a straight line. Every engagement starts with a free on-site assessment; call (978) 307-8107.

mainEntity.name: Which Littleton ZIP codes do you cover?

acceptedAnswer.text: All of them: 01460. If your facility sits on a town line, tell us the street address and we will confirm.

mainEntity.name: Which nearby towns do you also serve?

acceptedAnswer.text: The closest served towns to Littleton are Boxborough (about 3.8 mi), Westford (about 4.3 mi), Acton (about 4.5 mi). See the full list on our service areas page.

mainEntity.name: These units are our residents' homes, not hospital rooms. How do your staff work inside them?

acceptedAnswer.text: Legally and practically that distinction governs everything. Our staff knock and wait, announce themselves, work on a published schedule the resident knows in advance, and never move or discard personal belongings — anything unclear is left in place and reported to your staff, not decided by a cleaner. We do not open drawers, closets or medication storage. If a resident declines service that day, we log the refusal and leave; we do not negotiate with them. Staff assigned to residences are consistent week to week, because a familiar face in a memory care wing prevents far more incidents than any protocol document.

mainEntity.name: Our compliance review is coming up. What do the state reviewers look at that touches housekeeping?

acceptedAnswer.text: Under 651 CMR 12.09, Massachusetts compliance reviews occur at least every two years and must include a physical inspection of the residence's common areas — dining, activity and lounge spaces, corridors, common bathrooms, laundry and trash rooms. Those are the areas where a reviewer forms an impression in the first ten minutes. We keep them on a named schedule rather than an as-available one, with logs showing frequency, and we walk them with your Executive Director before the review window opens. Anything requiring paint, flooring, upholstery replacement or repair goes to you in writing with enough lead time to act.

mainEntity.name: How do you know your staff are actually observing disinfectant contact times?

acceptedAnswer.text: A CDC assessment of 438 long-term care facilities in 2020 found 18.1% were unaware of the contact time for the disinfectants they were using — and 206 of those facilities were assisted living. The failure mode is wiping a surface that dries in thirty seconds when the label requires several minutes, so the kill claim is never met. We standardize on a short product list, print the contact time on the bottle label and the cart, train to that number, and check it during supervisor rounds by asking the cleaner to state it. If a surface dries early it is re-wetted, not counted.

Assisted Living & Senior Living Cleaning for Littleton facilities

In a assisted living residence, most cleaning failures happen at residential units, common areas, memory care wings. That is where our Littleton crews start, because the underlying risk is vulnerable population in what is legally their home, not a clinical setting.

How we clean assisted living residences in Littleton

High-touch surfaces on every visit

  • Common-room seating
  • Dining tables and chairs
  • Handrails
  • Elevator buttons
  • Kitchenette surfaces in apartments (as contracted)
  • Mailroom and lobby counters

What the crew does, in order

  1. Enter resident apartments only with permission and at the time agreed.
  2. Escalate cleaning during respiratory or gastrointestinal illness as directed by the residence.
  3. Keep laundry and food-service areas to their own cleaning procedures.
  4. Damp-mop floors with wet-floor signage to reduce fall risk.
  5. Log apartments and common areas completed.

A starting schedule

  • Resident apartments: per service plan, commonly weekly.
  • Illness outbreaks: escalated as the residence directs.
  • Periodic: carpets, windows and high dusting.

Apartment housekeeping days are usually fixed so residents know when to expect the team.

Documentation you receive

  • Common-area schedule
  • Apartment housekeeping checklist
  • Signed service logs
  • Certificate of insurance

Survey findings we help Littleton facilities prevent

Real, published regulatory findings — every citation links to its source.

CDC Infection Control Assessment and Response (ICAR)

No auditing of hand hygiene and PPE compliance — a written policy exists, but no observational monitoring confirms staff follow it.

16.8% of the same 438 facilities did no such auditing. Assisted living performed materially worse than nursing homes on several controls in that study.

29 CFR 1910.1030 — OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens

Bloodborne pathogens programme deficiencies — exposure control plan, contaminated laundry, regulated waste, surface decontamination and PPE.

Federal OSHA, October 2024 to September 2025: 9 citations across 3 inspections of assisted living facilities, carrying $37,006 in penalties — the largest penalty total of any standard for the sector.

651 CMR 12.04(1)(e) and 651 CMR 12.04(13)(b)1

Failure to meet the State Sanitary Code. This is an express condition of certification for every Massachusetts assisted living residence, and a sponsor must forward any Sanitary Code, Building Code or fire safety citation it receives to the state within seven days.

See all 6 findings
